summary.text: 米 is a whole-graph picture of scattered grain. Its early referent was probably dehusked grain broadly; today it commonly means rice. The central stroke’s identity is disputed.

formation.text: Pictographic (象形): the marks around a central stroke depict scattered grain. The overall picture does not depend on identifying the central stroke, which has been interpreted as either a sieve or a grain stalk.

history.text: Early forms are described as small marks above and below a central stroke. The selected oracle-bone-style image is a modern redraw; it illustrates that description but is not an ancient inscription. Forms are also listed for Chu manuscripts, bronze inscriptions, small seal script, and the Shuowen entry. One account says the dots were joined into strokes before the small-seal form, with Chu examples showing that this change had already begun. These descriptions do not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes.
The Shuowen entry explains 米 as grain seed or fruit and says the graph depicts the fruit of grain plants. This is an early dictionary interpretation of the graph’s form.

uncertainties.text: The central stroke has been interpreted as a sieve or a grain stalk; it may instead be a graphic separator. Its identity remains unresolved, but the uncertainty does not affect the overall reading as a picture of grain.
The exact dates and contexts of the reported early uses are unresolved, as is the chronology by which the broad grain sense came to be commonly rice-specific.

senses.text: The cited account reports oracle-bone use for rice or grain; scholarly discussion identifies the early referent as probably dehusked grain broadly, rather than one particular crop. The precise first-use date and inscription context are unresolved.
In common modern usage, 米 means rice.

In Japanese, 米 is used for the length unit metre after 米突 served as a sound-based rendering of French mètre. The metre use is unrelated in meaning to grain. The exact route by which 米 alone became current is unresolved.

developments.text: The broad early grain sense is commonly specialized to rice in modern usage, though the chronology of this change is unresolved.

米突 represented French mètre by sound, and 米 was later used as a shorter written form for the unit. This borrowed word is unrelated in meaning to grain; the date and precise route by which the shorter form became current are unresolved.

limitations.text: Other reported early uses include writing 敉 ‘pacify’, a sacrificial name, and clan names. Their inscription contexts and relationship, if any, to the grain meaning are unresolved, so they are not treated here as semantic developments or separate senses.
Additional Japanese readings are listed, but their senses and histories are not explained here; the metre use is the one supported by the cited account.

items.period: Shang dynasty script style (image is a modern redraw)
items.caption: This modern redraw presents 米 in an oracle-bone script style: small marks are arranged around a central stroke, a form associated with a pictograph of scattered grain. The central stroke has been interpreted as a sieve or as a grain stalk.
items.alt: Black oracle-bone-style marks: three short strokes above and three below a long diagonal stroke.
items.selection_reason: The grain-like arrangement illustrates the pictographic explanation, while the accompanying limitation keeps the disputed interpretation of the central stroke clear.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the file description page; modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw in an oracle-bone script style, not an image of an excavated inscription. The arrangement supports the grain pictograph interpretation but does not resolve whether the central stroke represents a sieve, a stalk, or another feature.
